complexity.correctness_reason: numpy's int64 overflows once n exceeds 92 (F(93) > 2^63), producing wrapped negative values as soon as the n <= 45 cap is lifted.
complexity.notes: The reported O(log n) is unit-cost arithmetic; the Fibonacci values have Θ(n) bits, so the true bit-level cost of the big multiplications is higher — worth knowing, though digit work is never folded into the reported figure. Pulling in numpy for a two-line recurrence is a heavy dependency, and it is also the source of the correctness issue: numpy uses fixed-width int64, so the result silently wraps once F(n) exceeds 2^63. A pure-Python version of the same matrix power (or any fast doubling) uses arbitrary-precision ints and would be correct for all n at the same unit-cost complexity.
complexity.summary: Computes the n-th Fibonacci number by raising the 2x2 transition matrix [[1,1],[1,0]] to the n-th power with numpy's binary-exponentiation matrix_power.
